source.attribution: Inferred from the official 2025-present moderator listing and the dominant accepting moderator in the recent request sample.
source.storage: Aggregated guidance only; no private record text or conversation corpus is stored.

principles: Open with a short thank-you for the submission or for the author's latest message.
Bundle all requested changes into one reply and group them under field headings.
Use a polite direct request and explain the reason only when it helps the author act.
Ask the author to reply in the Conversation area after making changes.
For follow-ups, acknowledge completed changes before naming anything still missing.
When scope is uncertain, ask for clarification before performing the full metadata review.
Do not chase authors with reminders; wait for their reply.
Treat PDF/A as a preference, not a publication blocker.
Ask for README.md, README.txt, or files_description.md alongside uploaded archives, not only inside them.
Handle a DOI written as a URL as a moderator-side metadata edit; do not ask the author to make that trivial correction.
Keep final accept, decline, and metadata-edit decisions human-controlled.

calibration.method: GET-only comparison with records accepted by moderator user 1965; aggregate results only.
schema_corrections: Use structured ref_link, DOI, URL, and ref_comment fields when reviewing references.
Decode HTML entities before checking the visible end punctuation of descriptions.
Treat software packaged in an archive as a human file-inspection question, not an automatic resource-type error.
calibration.caveat: Past acceptance is evidence, not an automatic approval label; scientific scope, file contents, exceptions, and every final decision still require a moderator.
